title: How To Make Your First Million Dollars (Charge A Premium!) ft. Myron Golden
summary: Myron Golden on a podcast: charge premium prices because rich people pay to solve problems, coaching repays its cost many times, and events sell back-end offers.

assertions.quote: happy as a lark in the park in the dark to pay whatever the price is to solve their problem.

verdicts.note: Some sellers underprice, but demand is price-sensitive for most offers; anecdotes of raised prices selling more are selected cases.

assertions.quote: I knew the price I was charging you was worth way was way less than the value that you were going to get.

verdicts.note: The returns cited are selected client testimonials; no independent data shows typical buyers recover high coaching fees.

assertions.quote: If you're not a premium buyer, you can't attract premium buyers.

verdicts.note: A motivational framing that also serves to sell the speaker's own premium coaching.

assertions.quote: Let's say you can get one out of 10, so you talk to 100 people, you can make 10 sales.
Every book I sell like at full price I am making a thousand percent return.

verdicts.note: Markup ignores overhead, marketing and capital at risk; it is not an annual return on invested capital and cannot be compared to market returns.

assertions.quote: If I spend an hour cutting some grass, I just flushed $40,000 of value down the toilet.
But then we sold another 700,000 dollars in offers on the back end.
